page: Microsoft Azure D192s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 vCPUs mapped to 96 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system includes 768.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8). This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 159,025.89 and a PassMark CPU score of 122,467.64. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, reaching 510.75 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 12,325.72 GB/sec for cached small-block reads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves a top-tier throughput of 868.96 GB/sec. For database workloads, the instance demonstrates strong capabilities, processing 173.14 million Redis SET operations per second and achieving top-tier PassMark database operation scores. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average tier.

The D192s_v6 offers high resource density for parallelized workloads, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for large-scale deployments that can leverage its 192 vCPUs. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on external Premium Storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage configuration. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though its AMX instructions support moderate CPU-based LLM inference, processing 7B model prompts at 266.18 tokens per second. This server is suited for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data processing.
